1) NE and NPY, administered peripherally, have synergistic effects on body weight, food intake and RMR in obese Zucker rats.
the combined treatment with NPY and NE causes significant weight loss in obese Zucker rats, and that BAT plays an important role in the metabolic response to this treatment.
chronic administration of NPY in combination with NE, in warm environmental conditions, caused significant weight reduction in obese Zucker rats.

the effect of NPY and NE administered separately or in combination, on the metabolic response in the obese Zucker rats.
the metabolic effects of NE and NPY on food intake, RMR and BAT activity in adult male obese (Zucker) rats in warm and cold environments.
the metabolic effects of NE and NPY in obese rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the peripheral administration of NYP enhances the metabolic action of norepinephrines on the obese Zucker rat.
the combined treatment with NPY and NE is more effective in the cold than in the warm environmental conditions.
the synergistic action between NPY and NE is a function of both central and peripheral nervous system, and is mediated through BAT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the peripheral action of NPY is to augment the action of NE on food intake, metabolism and BAT.
the peripheral administration of NYP and NE together causes a remarkable synergistic effect on food intake, body weight, and metabolic rate.

NPY and NE have additive effects on the thermogenic activity of the brown adipocytes and that the combined treatment of these hormones may have a therapeutic potential in the treatment of obesity in the obese (fat/fat) Zucker rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chronic peripheral administration of NE and NPY can cause significant weight loss by inhibiting food consumption and by increasing RMR.
the combined peripheral treatment of NE and NPY has a synergistic effect on the metabolic response of the obese rat.
the combined treatment with NPY and NE is more effective than the separate treatments in reducing total body weight in obese (fa/fa), Zucker rats.
